currentContext.business: Chemplast Sanmar manufactures and sells speciality and value-added chemicals from four Tamil Nadu / Puducherry sites, organised into five product domains: Speciality Paste PVC resin, Custom Manufactured Chemicals (starting materials, advanced intermediates and active ingredients for global originators), Hydrogen Peroxide, Caustic Soda and Chloromethanes, with Refrigerant Gas (R32) added as a new vertical. Suspension PVC is operated through its wholly owned subsidiary Chemplast Cuddalore Vinyls Limited (CCVL), India's second-largest S-PVC manufacturer and the largest in South India. The Company serves footwear, automotive and furniture upholstery, artificial leather, pharmaceutical, agrochemical, fine chemical, paper, textile, alumina, irrigation and construction customers in India and across a nine-country export presence.

Speciality Chemicals: Custom Manufactured Chemicals (CMCD) - starting materials, advanced intermediates, active ingredients
Value-added Chemicals: Chloromethanes - Methyl Chloride, Methylene Dichloride, Chloroform, Carbon Tetrachloride
Captive intermediates: Ethylene Dichloride (EDC) for captive use at Karaikal

currentContext.expansion: Chemplast Sanmar's expansion agenda runs across three speciality vectors. In Speciality Paste PVC, the previous year was about building capacity and 2025-26 was about executing on it: the 41 KTPA facility at Cuddalore achieved 100% utilisation in its very first full year of commercial operation, and management describes the market's rapid absorption of the new Cuddalore capacity as validating the expansion strategy. Building on that, the business has initiated debottlenecking of the Cuddalore unit, targeting an additional 6 KT of capacity through a low-investment route that materially enhances capital efficiency. In parallel, the business embarked on development of emulsion-based grades as a critical growth vector - key equipment required for emulsion PVC development was ordered during the year, and significant preparatory work has been completed towards an expansion roadmap for gaining more market share in the next few years. At Mettur, the Furnace Revamp Project was kicked off during the year and is expected to improve VCM productivity and operational reliability in the coming year, further strengthening backward integration and cost competitiveness. In Custom Manufactured Chemicals, capacity is being aggressively expanded at the Berigai multipurpose blocks: civil work for Phase 3 of Multipurpose Block MPB-3 is progressing well with full completion and pilot Phase 3 commissioning expected in the first quarter of 2026-27, while civil works for MPB-4 are advancing on track and are targeted for completion in the second quarter of 2026-27. Management expects that on a steady-state basis, past the initial learning curves of new product launches, CMCD EBITDA margins will settle in line with global industry standards. In Refrigerant Gas, the R32 HFC investment announced during 2025-26 progressed as planned and was expected to start production during 2026-27; subsequent to the close of the financial year, commercial production of R32 Refrigerant Gas from the Swing Plant at Mettur has commenced, timed to the final phase of the HCFC phase-out that is driving faster HFC demand in both OEM and service segments.
currentContext.mdna: Speciality Paste PVC: the Indian market of roughly 1,92,000 metric tons per annum is a structural growth story with demand growing steadily at 7% to 8%, fuelled by robust automotive and footwear demand; industry demand grew by approximately 15 KT in 2025-26.|A footwear-segment shift toward value-added products over low-quality mass offerings is expected to reshape the supplier landscape, influencing quality standards and volume requirements across the value chain.|Realisations are the key Paste PVC margin lever: management describes being 'on the verge of a regulatory reset that should structurally improve our realisations' once final ADD findings on EU and Japan imports land early in 2026-27.|Import bookings from Europe are already being held at significantly low levels by the impending DGTR determination, easing the pricing pressure that EU cross-subsidised exports created through most of 2025-26.|Deep backward integration is the stated buffer against feedstock volatility - variable margins held steady through the West Asia crisis feedstock shock.|CMCD: the 'China plus one' strategy is accelerating as global agrochemical majors diversify supply chains, but a China capacity overhang in low-priced generic active ingredients is temporarily reducing the incentive for innovators to switch to new, higher-cost chemistries, slowing new-molecule ramp-up.|CMCD margin path: on a steady-state basis, past the initial learning curves on new product launches, management anticipates EBITDA margins for this business to settle in line with global industry standards.|CMCD mix shift is the earnings-profile driver - management frames the business as transitioning the Company 'from a volume-driven model to a value-creation engine'.|Chloromethanes: excess domestic capacity and global margin pressure persist; MDC demand from large pharmaceutical customers is a reliable volume anchor, Chloroform pharma demand softened partly offset by UPR and footwear, and CTC demand from synthetic pyrethroid producers stayed weak on high agrochemical inventories and cheap Chinese imports.|Caustic Soda: India is structurally oversupplied (capacity around 6.3 Million tonnes against demand just under 5 Million tonnes) and pricing and margin pressures are expected to continue, but the product's regional nature and the surplus being concentrated in Western India give the Company's southern location a more balanced supply-demand dynamic.|Hydrogen Peroxide is integrated with caustic soda - volumes fell because lower Mettur caustic production reduced hydrogen feedstock availability; after the March 2026 West Asia gas-shortage price spike and subsequent demand collapse, the market is expected to gradually settle with near-term pricing sensitive to macro pressure and downstream raw-material constraints.|Suspension PVC: India's structural deficit (demand approximately 4.3 Million tonnes against domestic production of only 1.5 Million tonnes) means India will remain a net importer for the foreseeable future, providing a reliable market for the Company's output even as competitors add capacity.|S-PVC near-term outlook stays cautious - a marginal 1% decline in annual domestic demand, persistent dumping from the US and China (China alone roughly 52% to 54% of S-PVC imports into India), and delays in QCOs and ADDs, only partly offset by modest pricing recovery after China's withdrawal of its 13% export tax rebate effective April 01, 2026.|Management believes the third quarter of 2025-26 represented the absolute bottom of the PVC cycle.|R32 is a new topline driver: commercial production began in May 2026 at the 2 KTPA Mettur swing plant, described as the initiation of a highly profitable revenue stream that at targeted full capacity will add significantly to the topline.|Green power under the Group Captive scheme now contributes over 35% of total energy needs from renewables, structurally reducing the carbon footprint while delivering cost savings.|CMCD has successfully commercialised 17 products to date and maintains a robust, high-velocity pipeline of several more molecules under development.|The Managing Director states the pipeline carries 17 commercialised products with over 45 molecules at various stages of development.|Business development engine remains highly active with new product leads and customer engagements progressing strongly across global markets; senior business development resources added in Europe and Japan to diversify the customer base.|CMCD conversion target: turn the extensive molecule pipeline into contracted revenue using the newly commissioned phases of the Multipurpose Blocks.

risks.risk: Feedstock and commodity cycle vulnerability (Strategic and Market Risk)
risks.note: Volatility in pricing of key feedstocks such as Ethylene, EDC and Methanol, along with finished commodities like S-PVC, can lead to margin fluctuations and earnings instability, particularly during geopolitical disruptions. Mitigation rests on leveraging deep backward integration to capture value across the chain and on structurally reducing dependence on cyclical commodity segments by strengthening the higher-margin CMCD and Paste PVC businesses, with further investment in Refrigerant Gases broadening the speciality portfolio.

risks.risk: Unfair trade practices and dumping into the Indian market, compounded by the withdrawal of non-tariff safeguards
risks.note: Dumping by international players can impact profitability and market competitiveness. The Quality Control Order was withdrawn in Quarter 3, removing quality thresholds for overseas suppliers, and imports from the US and China entered at low prices. The Company engages actively with regulatory authorities to support timely implementation of Anti-Dumping Duties to safeguard domestic markets. Management has taken the dumping issue up with the Government.

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation exposure (Financial and Trade Risk)
risks.note: Exposure to foreign exchange volatility, particularly USD/INR, can impact profitability. Managed through a disciplined, Board-approved forex hedging framework supported by natural hedges from export growth in CMCD.

risks.risk: Global supply chain fragmentation (Operational and Supply Chain Risk)
risks.note: Freight rate volatility, geopolitical disruptions and logistical bottlenecks can impact raw material availability and timely delivery of finished goods. The US-Iran war disrupted feedstock supply chains, triggering force majeure declarations by Asian producers and tightening ethylene availability, increasing input costs. Mitigated by a geographically diversified vendor base, long-term freight contracts, and advanced demand planning and inventory optimisation models.

risks.risk: Process safety and environmental compliance (EHS Risk)
risks.note: Chemical manufacturing operations carry inherent environment, health and safety risks that could lead to operational disruptions, regulatory actions or reputational impact if not effectively managed. Mitigated through globally benchmarked Process Safety Management systems, detailed HAZOP studies for new processes, and Zero Liquid Discharge facilities.

risks.risk: Data and intellectual property security (Information Technology and Cyber Risk)
risks.note: Increasing digitalisation and growth in CMCD heighten the risk of data breaches and potential compromise of proprietary client intellectual property - a direct threat to the CMCD franchise, which is built on a confidentiality-led 'One Product, One Customer' model. Mitigation includes strengthening cybersecurity infrastructure with advanced threat detection systems and segregated environments.

risks.risk: Integration cascade risk across the value chain
risks.note: The integrated model means operational constraints in one segment propagate downstream: baseline Hydrogen Peroxide volumes declined this year as a direct consequence of technical issues and lower Caustic Soda production at Mettur, which temporarily reduced availability of the critical hydrogen feedstock.

risks.risk: Sustained margin pressure and cycle-low pricing in the commodity segments
risks.note: S-PVC, Caustic Soda and Chloromethanes absorbed the full impact of global dumping and cycle-low pricing, and CMCD was impacted by the global agrochemicals slowdown. Management expects margin pressure for Suspension PVC to persist for some more time, with improvement expected over the later part of financial year 2026-27.

risks.risk: Increasingly stringent emission and environmental regulatory standards
risks.note: BRSR flags that the financial implications of complying with future, more stringent standards may be significant. The Company positions itself ahead of the curve through ZLD plants across all sites, desalination plants at coastal locations, Responsible Care(R) certification, low-sulphur coal at its thermal power plant, and biomass blending, so that it is not taken by surprise by new regulations.

BRSR identifies improper disposal of waste by third parties as a material issue. Mitigated by disposing only to authorised recyclers and ensuring proper disposal through documentation and periodic verification by auditing the facilities.

one-line thesis: Chemplast Sanmar reported a consolidated net loss of INR 280 crores for FY26, driven by a massive INR 898 crore non-cash impairment on its CCVL (Suspension PVC) subsidiary due to collapsed spreads from Chinese dumping and war-induced feedstock volatility. While the commodity business faces structural distress requiring potential reorganization or M&A, the Specialty and CDMO segments remain resilient with a strong order book, positioning the company for a pivot toward higher-margin fluoropolymers and custom synthesis in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 4,224 cr (FY26), INR 1,256 cr (Q4, +9% YoY); EBITDA: INR 198 cr (FY26), INR 194 cr (Q4 vs INR 37 cr YoY); PAT: Net Loss INR 280 cr (FY26), Net Loss INR 45 cr (Q4) - impacted by INR 898 cr impairment (CCVL investment) and INR 150 cr exceptional charge (onerous contracts/inventory write-down); Order Book: Strong in CDMO (45+ molecules, 17 commercial), Neutral/Weak in SPVC; Net Debt: INR 1,419 cr (Consolidated). One-offs: INR 898 cr impairment (non-cash, stand-alone P&L impact), INR 150 cr inventory/contract provision (expected reversal in FY27).
guidance: Revenue Growth: CDMO target of INR 1,000 cr delayed by ~12 months, now expected in FY27; Margin: SPVC spreads currently at breakeven/variable cost level, contingent on 7.5% customs duty reinstatement (expected end-June 2026) and geopolitical stabilization; Order Inflow: CDMO pipeline growing quarter-on-quarter despite agrochemical slowdown; Capex/Commissioning: R32 capacity to reach 14 kt by end-CY2026; MPB Phase III progressing.
order book & pipeline: CDMO: 45+ molecules in pipeline (17 commercial, 6 with LOIs); SPVC: Muted demand (~4.3 Mn tons domestic market), pricing pressure from Chinese imports at $820/ton CFR India.
segment / subsidiary detail: Specialty (Paste PVC): Revenue INR 475 cr (Q4, +13% YoY), volumes +17% YoY; Cuddalore facility at 100% capacity; ADD on EU/Japan imports finalized, awaiting notification. CDMO: Impacted by global agrochemical slowdown and delayed new molecule ramp-ups; hiring senior resources in Europe/Japan. Value-Added (Caustic/Chloromethanes): Revenue INR 120 cr (Q4, down from INR 169 cr YoY); volumes impacted by Mettur membrane change; prices stabilizing post-war spike. Suspension PVC (CCVL): Revenue INR 661 cr (Q4, +18% YoY) but margins crushed by VCM-PVC spread inversion; INR 150 cr exceptional charge taken.
growth verticals / optionality: R32 Refrigerant Gas: 2 kt swing plant commissioned, expanding to 14 kt by end-2026; targeting domestic and export markets (quota allocation expected by 2027). CDMO: Diversification beyond agrochemicals into pharma/specialty intermediates; potential revenue pool from 45-molecule pipeline. Strategic Review: Board committee formed to explore reorganization, demerger, or M&A to unlock value between high-growth Specialty and distressed Commodity assets.
margins & cost dynamics: SPVC spreads at neutral/breakeven on replacement cost basis; VCM prices volatile due to Middle East conflict (naphtha/ethylene shortage); Chinese carbide PVC flooding market at low costs. Caustic soda power-intensive; JSW renewable power JV benefits VAC more than SPVC. Feedstock security for R32 (HF) secured via third-party ties, logistics being scaled.
capex / expansion: R32 expansion to 14 kt capacity; MPB Phase III (CDMO) ongoing; Mettur membrane replacement completed. Focus on debottlenecking and swing capacity utilization rather than greenfield commodity expansion.
capital allocation: Board constituted a committee of independent directors to evaluate strategic priorities, potential reorganization, and M&A opportunities to enhance long-term value. Impairment of INR 898 cr aligns book value with economic reality, no cash impact. Debt reduction contingent on commodity cycle recovery or asset restructuring.
risks & watch-items: Prolonged Chinese dumping of PVC nullifying regulatory relief; Failure of government to reinstate 7.5% customs duty or implement ADD on Chinese SPVC; Geopolitical escalation disrupting VCM/energy supply; CDMO pipeline ramp-up delays beyond FY27; R32 quota allocation uncertainty (though management confident).
management quality / tone: Candid on commodity distress ('structural reset', 'chaotic situation'); Defensive on impairment ('accounting entry', 'no cash impact'); Optimistic on Specialty/CDMO fundamentals ('strong order book', 'bullish medium-term'); Strategic ambiguity on restructuring ('clean slate', 'evaluate reorganization').
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 898 cr impairment is on the parent's investment in CCVL, not a consolidated P&L charge, yet it drives the standalone net loss of INR 1,003 cr; Management explicitly flagged a 'strategic review' committee, hinting at a potential demerger of the toxic SPVC asset from the high-value Specialty/CDMO business to re-rate the stock; The R32 export strategy relies on anticipated HFC quotas which are not yet formally allocated but expected by 2027.

growth verticals / optionality: R32 Refrigerant Gas: 2 kt swing plant commissioned, expanding to 14 kt by end-2026; targeting domestic and export markets (quota allocation expected by 2027). CDMO: Diversification beyond agrochemicals into pharma/specialty intermediates; potential revenue pool from 45-molecule pipeline. Strategic Review: Board committee formed to explore reorganization, demerger, or M&A to unlock value between high-growth Specialty and distressed Commodity assets.
margins & cost dynamics: SPVC spreads at neutral/breakeven on replacement cost basis; VCM prices volatile due to Middle East conflict (naphtha/ethylene shortage); Chinese carbide PVC flooding market at low costs. Caustic soda power-intensive; JSW renewable power JV benefits VAC more than SPVC. Feedstock security for R32 (HF) secured via third-party ties, logistics being scaled.
capex / expansion: R32 expansion to 14 kt capacity; MPB Phase III (CDMO) ongoing; Mettur membrane replacement completed. Focus on debottlenecking and swing capacity utilization rather than greenfield commodity expansion.
capital allocation: Board constituted a committee of independent directors to evaluate strategic priorities, potential reorganization, and M&A opportunities to enhance long-term value. Impairment of INR 898 cr aligns book value with economic reality, no cash impact. Debt reduction contingent on commodity cycle recovery or asset restructuring.
risks & watch-items: Prolonged Chinese dumping of PVC nullifying regulatory relief; Failure of government to reinstate 7.5% customs duty or implement ADD on Chinese SPVC; Geopolitical escalation disrupting VCM/energy supply; CDMO pipeline ramp-up delays beyond FY27; R32 quota allocation uncertainty (though management confident).
management quality / tone: Candid on commodity distress ('structural reset', 'chaotic situation'); Defensive on impairment ('accounting entry', 'no cash impact'); Optimistic on Specialty/CDMO fundamentals ('strong order book', 'bullish medium-term'); Strategic ambiguity on restructuring ('clean slate', 'evaluate reorganization').
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 898 cr impairment is on the parent's investment in CCVL, not a consolidated P&L charge, yet it drives the standalone net loss of INR 1,003 cr; Management explicitly flagged a 'strategic review' committee, hinting at a potential demerger of the toxic SPVC asset from the high-value Specialty/CDMO business to re-rate the stock; The R32 export strategy relies on anticipated HFC quotas which are not yet formally allocated but expected by 2027.

| Chinese carbide PVC dumping and inverted VCM-PVC spreads crushing domestic producers | Finolex Industries | beneficiary | Med | Pure-play PVC peer may benefit if anti-dumping duties are finally enforced, though currently facing same margin pressure; Chemplast's distress highlights sector-wide need for protection. |

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
